context.text: A clothing shop sold three lines of shirts last month.

context.title: Shirt sales

prompt: What was the average selling price of a shirt?
shortcut: Weight by shirts sold; the plain average of the three prices ($28.33) overweights the linen line.

context.text: A team of 8 consultants bills an average of 1,450 hours a year each. Two new consultants join, and each is expected to bill 1,200 hours a year.

prompt: What will the team's average billed hours per consultant be?
shortcut: The two newcomers are 250 hours below; spread 2 × 250 = 500 over 10 people: 50 below 1,450.

context.text: A bakery's website took 500 orders over five days, with an average order value of $48 across all of them. Day 5 had 100 orders.

context.title: Days 1 to 4

prompt: What was the average order value on day 5?
shortcut: Work in gaps from $48: day 1 is 120 × −4, day 2 80 × +4, day 3 100 × −2, day 4 100 × +2, a net −160 that day 5 must make up: +1.60 on 100 orders.

context.text: A delivery fleet has 60 diesel vans that use 9 litres of fuel per 100 km and 40 hybrid vans that use 6 litres per 100 km. Every van drives the same distance.

prompt: What is the fleet's average fuel use per 100 km driven?
shortcut: Weights 60:40 pull the average 40% of the way from 9 to 6: 9 − 1.2 = 7.8.

context.text: A truck drives 120 km to a customer at an average of 60 km/h, and returns the same 120 km in heavy traffic at an average of 40 km/h.

prompt: What is the truck's average speed for the round trip?
solution: Time out: 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours; time back: 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours
shortcut: Average speed is total distance over total time; the slow leg takes longer, so the answer sits below the plain average of 50.

context.text: A manufacturer scores its suppliers out of 100 using a weighted scorecard.

context.title: Supplier scorecard

prompt: What is the supplier's overall weighted score?
shortcut: Weight each score; the plain average (82.3) ignores that quality, the weakest score, counts for half.

context.text: A department store reports sales and gross margin by category.

context.title: Sales mix and margins

prompt: What is the store's overall gross margin?
shortcut: Margins average by sales weight; the simple average of 12, 45 and 30 (29%) overweights apparel.

context.text: A cosmetics company sells a mass-market range at a 20% margin and a premium range at a 50% margin. Last year the mass range was 70% of revenue and premium 30%. This year the split is 55% mass and 45% premium, and each range's margin is unchanged.

prompt: By how many percentage points did the company's overall margin change?
shortcut: 15 points of mix moved from a 20% range to a 50% range: 0.15 × 30 = 4.5 points.

context.text: A coffee roaster blends Arabica beans costing $9 per kg with Robusta beans costing $5 per kg. It wants its espresso blend to cost $7.40 per kg.

prompt: What percentage of the blend, by weight, must be Arabica?
solution: Let a be the Arabica share: 9a + 5(1 − a) = 7.40
shortcut: The target sits 2.40 of the 4.00 gap above Robusta: 2.4 ÷ 4 = 60% Arabica.

context.text: A garden centre has two branches. Last month the town branch served 400 customers with an average spend of $50, and the out-of-town branch served 100 customers with an average spend of $90. Next month the out-of-town branch expects to serve twice as many customers, with the same average spend, while the town branch stays the same.

prompt: What will the average spend per customer be across both branches next month?
shortcut: One third of customers spend $40 more than the rest: $50 + $40 ÷ 3 ≈ $63.33.

context.text: A frozen-yoghurt franchise has 40 outlets with average annual revenue of $1.25m each. Outlets come in three formats. There are 5 flagship outlets.

context.title: Average annual revenue by format

prompt: How many kiosk outlets does the franchise have?
solution: The other 35 outlets earn $35m, an average of $1.0m
shortcut: If all 35 were standard they would earn $42m; each kiosk is $0.5m less, and the shortfall is $7m: 7 ÷ 0.5 = 14.

context.text: A hotel group has three loans outstanding.

context.title: Loans

prompt: What is the group's average interest rate on its debt, weighted by amount?
shortcut: Total interest over total debt; the simple average of the three rates (6.3%) overweights the small mezzanine loan.

context.text: On one route an airline sells economy seats at $150 and premium seats at $400, prices it has not changed in two years. Last year 12% of passengers flew premium, and average revenue per passenger was $180. This year average revenue per passenger rose to $189.

prompt: What share of passengers flew premium this year?
shortcut: Each point of premium share adds $2.50 to the average; $189 is $39 above the economy fare: 39 ÷ 2.5 = 15.6. Scaling 12% by 189 ÷ 180 gives 12.6%, the trap.

context.text: A utility's call centre sorts its calls into two types: 70% are simple calls lasting 4 minutes on average, and 30% are complex calls lasting 11 minutes. A new self-service app is expected to remove half of the simple calls and none of the complex ones.

prompt: What will the average call length be once the app is live?
solution: Per 100 calls today: 70 simple and 30 complex; after the app, 35 simple and 30 complex
shortcut: Removing short calls raises the average; recompute on the new counts. Today's average (6.1) and the plain average of 4 and 11 (7.5) are both traps.

context.text: A regional airline aims to have 85% of its 48,000 flights this year arrive on time. From January to August it operated 31,500 flights, and 82% of them arrived on time.

prompt: What on-time rate does it need on its remaining flights to hit the annual target?
shortcut: The first 31,500 flights fell 3 points short; the other 16,500 must make that up: 85% + 3% × 31.5 ÷ 16.5 ≈ 85% + 5.7%. Mirroring the shortfall (88%) ignores the unequal sizes.

context.text: A packaging supplier prices each order on a sliding scale.

items: First 1,000 units of an order: $8 each

prompt: Which is closest to the average price per unit on an order of 8,000 units?
shortcut: Weight each band's price by its units (1 : 4 : 3), not equally; the simple average of the three prices is $6.50.

context.text: A kitchen-equipment distributor sold two product lines with combined sales of $5m and an overall margin of 18% (total profit divided by total sales). The commercial line earned a 12% margin and the domestic line a 30% margin.

prompt: What were the domestic line's sales?
solution: With domestic sales d: 0.12 × (5 − d) + 0.30 × d = 0.9, so 0.6 + 0.18d = 0.9
shortcut: The average sits 6 points above 12% and 12 points below 30%, so sales split 2 : 1 commercial to domestic; a third of $5m.

context.text: A bank expects a share of each type of loan to default each year.

context.title: Loan book

prompt: By approximately what percentage will the bank's expected default rate across the whole book rise from today to next year?
shortcut: Moving 10 points of book from a 1% to a 6% product adds 0.5 points on a 2.7% base: 0.5 ÷ 2.7 ≈ 18.5%. The 0.5 is a point change, not the percentage.

context.text: Your client is a professional ice hockey league of 16 clubs, which it groups as Small-Market Clubs, Mid-Market Clubs and Large-Market Clubs. Taking the league as a whole, a club averages $24 million of revenue and $1.1 million of profit a season.

context.title: Profile of the client's clubs (average per club)

prompt: Assume the league has 5 Small-Market Clubs. How many of its clubs are Large-Market Clubs?
solution: Each game one club wins is a game another club loses, so across the league clubs win 50% of their games
Mid-Market Clubs sit at 50%, so Small-Market and Large-Market Clubs must balance: 5 × (50% − 38%) = X × (70% − 50%), so 60 = 20X and X = 3
Check with revenue: 5 × 15 + 8 × 19 + 3 × 52 = $383 million, and $383 million ÷ 16 ≈ $23.9 million a club, in line with the $24 million average
shortcut: Small-Market Clubs are 12 points below 50% and Large-Market Clubs 20 points above, so 5 × 12 = X × 20 and X = 3.

context.text: The client runs the top men's volleyball division in its country. The division has 14 teams in three tiers: Small-Town Teams, Mid-Size City Teams and Big-City Teams. On average a team in the division brings in $7 million of revenue and $0.35 million of profit.

context.title: Breakdown of the division (average per team)

prompt: If 2 of the teams in the division are Small-Town Teams, how many Big-City Teams does it contain?
solution: Every match has one winner and one loser, so the division as a whole wins 50% of its matches
With the Mid-Size City Teams at 50%, the Small-Town and Big-City Teams must offset each other: 2 × (50% − 40%) = X × (55% − 50%), so 20 = 5X and X = 4
Check with revenue: 2 × 2.5 + 8 × 4 + 4 × 15 = $97 million, and $97 million ÷ 14 ≈ $6.9 million a team, close to the $7 million average
shortcut: Small-Town Teams are 10 points under 50% and Big-City Teams 5 points over, so 2 × 10 = X × 5 and X = 4.

context.text: The client is a professional rugby league with 20 teams of three kinds: Town Teams, County Teams and Metro Teams. League-wide, revenue averages $16 million per team and profit $0.9 million.

context.title: Team types in the league (average per team)

prompt: Suppose the league includes 6 Town Teams. How many of the league's teams are Metro Teams?
solution: Each game won by one team is lost by another, so the league as a whole wins 50% of its games
County Teams are at 50%, so Town and Metro Teams must cancel out: 6 × (50% − 44%) = X × (59% − 50%), so 36 = 9X and X = 4
Check with revenue: 6 × 8 + 10 × 12 + 4 × 39 = $324 million, and $324 million ÷ 20 ≈ $16.2 million a team, close to the $16 million average
shortcut: Town Teams are 6 points below 50% and Metro Teams 9 points above, so 6 × 6 = X × 9 and X = 4.

context.text: The client is a professional baseball league of 12 teams, grouped as Small-Market Teams, Mid-Market Teams and Big-Market Teams. Its average team brings in $68.5 million of revenue and $4.15 million of profit a year.

context.title: Segments of the client's league (average per team)

prompt: If the league has 3 Small-Market Teams, how many teams belong to the Big-Market segment?
solution: A win for one team is a loss for another, so the league's overall winning percentage is 50%
Mid-Market Teams are at 50%, so the other two segments must balance: 3 × (50% − 38%) = X × (59% − 50%), so 36 = 9X and X = 4
Check with revenue: 3 × 34 + 5 × 56 + 4 × 110 = $822 million, and $822 million ÷ 12 = $68.5 million a team
shortcut: Small-Market Teams are 12 points below 50% and Big-Market Teams 9 points above, so 3 × 12 = X × 9 and X = 4.

context.text: Timberline Mills (TM) saws logs into building timber and runs several sawmills. The log yard at its Mill 2 takes deliveries from 6am to 3pm, Monday to Friday.

context.title: Chart A: Logs delivered on each day of the week (Mill 2 log yard)

prompt: Which of the following values best approximates the tonnage of logs delivered to the Mill 2 yard on an average day from Monday to Friday?
shortcut: Tuesday to Friday each sit near 2,000 tonnes (about 7,800 together) and Monday adds about 350, so roughly 8,150 over 5 days, about 1,630 a day. Dividing by 7 gives the 1,165 option.

shortcut: Tuesday to Friday are each near 3,000 (about 11,500 together) and Monday adds about 5,600, so roughly 17,000 over 5 days, about 3,400 a day. Dividing by 7 gives the 2,445 option.

context.text: Goldmill Flour (GF) grinds wheat into flour for bakeries and owns three mills. Its main mill takes in wheat from 7am to 4pm Monday to Friday.

context.title: Chart A: Wheat taken in on each day of the week (GF main mill)

prompt: Which of the following values best approximates how much wheat the main mill takes in on a typical day from Monday to Friday, on average?
shortcut: Mon + Tue come to about 1,550, Wed + Thu about 1,550 and Fri about 1,600: roughly 4,700 tonnes, which over 5 days (not 7) is about 940 a day.

context.text: Partline Auto (PA) distributes car parts to independent garages. Its central warehouse accepts deliveries from suppliers between 7am and 3pm, Monday to Friday.

shortcut: Mon + Fri come to about 1,200, Tue + Thu about 1,500 and Wed about 850: roughly 3,550 pallets, which over 5 days (not 7) is about 710 a day.
